mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets the model invent an unauthenticated Operation whose outcome is Accepted, which is exactly the auth-bypass case FR-001 and the AuthRequiredEverywhere pattern are meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthAccepted { some op: Operation | op.auth = Unauthenticated and op.outcome = Accepted }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets an Accepted DeleteTask operation exist without a matching DeletionLog row, violating the one-log-per-deletion contract required by FR-018 and FR-012.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMissing { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteTask and op.outcome = Accepted and (no log: DeletionLog | log.forOp = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets two distinct DeletionLog rows reference the same Operation, which models a log row being rewritten or duplicated — the exact behaviour the append-only contract on task_deletions forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj l1, l2: DeletionLog | l1.forOp = l2.forOp }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a DeletionLog record a deleter who is not the actor of the operation it corresponds to — i.e. the log misattributes the action to the wrong member.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_Misattribution { some log: DeletionLog | log.deleter != log.forOp.actor }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets Alloy give two structurally identical authenticated operations different outcomes — an implicit role/permission distinction that the flat-peer spec (Q3 = A) forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_RoleSplit { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.auth = Authenticated and op2.auth = Authenticated and op1.kind = op2.kind and op1.target = op2.target and op1.newStatus = op2.newStatus and op1.outcome != op2.outcome }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets an EditTask operation on a Done task succeed without simultaneously reopening it (no newStatus set), violating the closed-task PATCH rule in FR-011.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedEditNoReopen { some op: Operation | op.kind = EditTask and op.outcome = Accepted and some op.target and op.target.status = Done and no op.newStatus }
